title: Short-power six-edge Stage G integration
objective: Rebuild the frozen splitting-degree catalog with the pending short-power loop proofs; require exactly six authenticated direct copy sites; replay all valid and malformed fixtures; and record paired timing and code-size evidence

handoff.summary: The isolated driver proves and requires exactly six authenticated unconditional direct-copy origins and replays all four frozen packets plus nine malformed controls. The first same-tip integration is deliberately rejected: whole-state scalar-summary provenance materializes 22 descriptor locals across four ordinary private helpers, adds 13,448 linked text bytes, and is 6.22% slower over 14/14 unfavorable paired measurements. Raw samples, artifact hashes, source snapshot hashes, diagnosis, and exact reproduction commands are checked in.
risks: The compiler input was an intentionally dirty integration worktree. Generated core, object, and addon hashes are authoritative; the evidence records the captured dirty source hashes and explicitly notes that the live worktree later changed.

The --record-rejected-materialization option exists only to reproduce the exact rejected 22/11/11/11 descriptor/data/length/offset census. The default path retains and currently fails the zero-descriptor acceptance gate.
No cross-platform claim is made for the benchmark numbers; this is a Linux x64 rejection diagnostic.
next_steps: After the compiler tracks summary provenance per scalar fact or argument, rerun the default driver without --record-rejected-materialization and require zero descriptor locals before timing.
Replace this negative evidence with a same-tip qualified six-edge report only if exact replay, code-shape gates, and paired timing all pass.
